newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures ends down despite buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures ends down despite buying.

text.p: Rubber futures finished lower on Tuesday despite light shortcovering by local buyers in a market slowly sliding into a stupor ahead of the Christmas holidays, dealers said.
"We did a bit of RSS3 and TSR20 rubber on some shortcovering. But the volumes were thin and as we get closer to Christmas, we'll just be singing Jingle Bells," a local rubber trader said.
The most actively traded month was the January and April/June RSS3 contracts where almost 800 tonnes each were traded in the local market.

About 600 tonnes of the April/June TSR20 contract was also traded. "The volumes involved today were not exciting. The market may drift further when the Christmas mood becomes more pronounced," another trader said.
At around 0945 GMT, January RSS3 was seen at 124.00-125.00 U.S. cents a kg compared with the previous 125.00 cents.
February RSS1 was seen at 179.00-181.00 Singapore cents (US$1.28-$1.29) a kg against 181.00 cents.
February TSR20 was seen at 173.00-174.00 Singapore cents (US$1.23-$1.24) a kg from 174.00 cents.
